predecessors.name: Four Oirats
predecessors.text: the steppe of Esen's empire outside the Oirat west: Mongolia, Inner Mongolia and the Manchurian guard lands

predecessors.name: Northern Yuan
predecessors.text: the Borjigin Great Khans' realm of 1368-1439

successors.name: Later Jin dynasty
successors.text: the Chakhar lands, whose khan Ejei 'surrendered to the Qing and gave the seal to Hong Taiji (February 1635)'

capitals.name: Eight White Yurts, Ordos (Dayan Khan's court)

ledger.x: 1455: Esen's death breaks the Oirat empire and the steppe passes to rival Mongol warlords and Borjigin khans.
1481: the Oirat west passes to the Great Khan's Mongols.
By 1495: the Three Guards join Dayan Khan's Mongols.
1500: Dayan Khan's court moves to the Eight White Yurts in the Ordos.
1500: the Mongols attack Ningxia from the Ordos.
1501: the court moves to the Kherlen River after a failed Ming counterattack.
1519: Cliopatria adds a strip of the Tian Shan foothills and Dzungaria (122,000 km2) from Moghulistan in the year Moghulistan splits in two.

1543: Dayan Khan dies after 'kept defeating the Ming in battle right up until his death in 1543' (Northern Yuan page; the Dayan Khan page has 'In 1542, Dayan Khan lost to Ming troops just before his death' and also dates his death to 1517).
1547: Altan takes the Right Wing and drives the Great Khan east.
1547: the Great Khan keeps only the east; the Khalkha lands of Mongolia pass to their own princes.
February 1635: the Chakhar lands pass to Hong Taiji's Later Jin (the Qing from 1636).
February 1635: the Mongol Khanate of the Great Khans ends with Ejei's surrender, 'ending the Kublaid descent ruled Northern Yuan'.

wars.name: Dayan Khan's reunification of the Mongols
wars.outcome: Dayan Khan unified the Eastern Mongols: a 1483 campaign against Ismayil Taishi, the Three Guards won by 1495, and the Three Right Wing Tumens crushed in 1510, when he killed Mandulai, the Ordos elder; the six tumens in a Left and a Right Wing.

wars.name: Mongol-Ming border wars under Dayan Khan
wars.outcome: Raids and invasions: pressure on the Ming from 1495, the attack on Ningxia in 1500 from the Ordos, forts at Xuanhua and Datong from 1513, invasions in 1514 and 1517 ('The high point of Mongol power came in 1517'), a defeat by Ming troops in 1542.

wars.name: Altan Khan's rise against the Great Khan
wars.outcome: Altan became leader of the Right Wing after 1542 and in 1547 forced Darayisung Khan to flee east; in 1551 Darayisung gave him the title Gegeen Khan.

wars.name: Ligdan Khan's war with the Later Jin and the Khorchin
wars.outcome: Ligdan attacked the Khorchin in 1624 and 1625 and beat them at Zhaocheng in 1628, but in 1632 Hong Taiji and his Mongol allies defeated the Chakhars and Ligdan fled to Qinghai, where he died of smallpox in 1634; Ejei surrendered in February 1635.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the Ming frontier (Ordos, Ningxia, Xuanhua, Datong) is a war zone with no treaty line.
